title: Steady-state steering: rate-limited regional failover with SLO-aware shedding
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and implement a steady-state steering policy that provides predictable failure behavior across regions while protecting latency SLOs. The policy should: 1) prefer local/low-latency regions when capacity and SLOs allow, 2) apply rate-limited failover credits to avoid thundering-herd effects during regional degradation, 3) integrate region-level circuit breakers and multi-tier load-shedding (model downgrade, partial response, reject), and 4) emit metrics and traces needed for per-tenant and per-route SLO analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Configurator exposes knobs: target_p99_latency_ms, region_capacity_quota, failover_credit_rate, circuit_breaker_open_threshold, load_shed_tiers
Requests are routed to preferred region when that region's p99 latency is <= target_p99 and free_capacity > region_capacity_quota
When a preferred region exceeds circuit-breaker thresholds, failover credits are consumed at a bounded rate (failover_credit_rate) rather than unbounded re-routing
Failover under sustained cross-region congestion follows tiered shedding: model-variant fallback -> partial response (truncated tokens + reason) -> 429/soft-reject depending on customer tier
Dashboards show per-region: request_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_cache_hit_ratio, free_capacity, circuit_breaker_state, failover_credit_balance
E2E canary (10% traffic) shows <5% regression in global p99 and no outage during injected regional failure tests
Automated rollback when circuit-breaker open rate or global p99 worsening exceeds configured alert thresholds
implementation_notes: Introduce a per-region token bucket (failover credit) funded by steady-state headroom. When local region opens, credits are consumed to allow limited cross-region routing.
Compute per-region free_capacity as: available_instances * concurrency_per_instance - inflight_requests_bound_by_kv_cache

Circuit breaker states: CLOSED, PROBING (sample 0.5% routed to region), OPEN (no new direct routes except via failover credits), HALF_OPEN (gradual probe). Use sliding-window error and latency metrics with adaptive thresholds.

Load-shed tiers implemented at router layer: prefer cheaper fallbacks before rejecting. Tier 1: route to quantized model variant; Tier 2: response truncation + metadata header 'x-shed-reason'; Tier 3: 429 with graceful message. Allow customer-level override for high-tier customers.
Routing decision order: region_affinity_hint -> capacity_check -> slo_check -> failover_credit_check -> final_route. Short-circuit order to minimize latency checks on the fast path.
Telemetry: emit trace span for routing decision with tags: chosen_region, candidate_regions, decision_reason, credit_before, credit_after, circuit_state
Backpressure study: instrument to capture re-dispatched requests to detect re-route loops and prevent oscillation by enforcing min_retarget_interval per request
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit tests + integration tests for token-bucket failover credits and circuit-breaker transitions (branch feature flag)
Phase 2: Internal canary to 1% of traffic in us-west region; monitor dashboards for 48h
Phase 3: 10% cross-region canary with synthetic regional degradation tests (delay/packet loss) and chaos experiments
Phase 4: Gradual ramp to 100% with kill-switch and fast rollback playbook; coordinate on-call and SRE for 24h post-ramp
Rollback criteria: sustained +10% increase in global p99 for 30m, credit exhaustion causing >1% 5xxs, or circuit oscillation >3 flips per hour
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit bucket arithmetic and concurrency corner cases
Simulation harness: 50k req/s replay to validate failover credit depletion behavior under different traffic skew patterns
Chaos monkey: simulate region network partition + injection of high-latency nodes while canary is active
Regression tests to ensure KV cache behavior does not inflate capacity estimates leading to premature shedding
Load tests for routing path extra-latency budget to measure added decision overhead (<1ms on p50)
Security review for any telemetry fields containing tenant identifiers (PII must be redacted)
Post-deploy SLO burn-down test: run weekly synthetic checks to ensure per-route p99 remains under target after 2 weeks
risks: Thundering herd during region failover if failover_credit_rate is set too high; mitigated via conservative defaults and telemetry alerts
Oscillation between regions when multiple regions are near capacity; mitigate with min_retarget_interval and hysteresis on p99 thresholds
Incorrect free_capacity estimates if KV cache eviction patterns change; require runtime metrics and alerts to detect estimation drift
Customer experience degradation for lower-tier customers due to aggressive shedding; ensure clear telemetry and opt-outs via customer config
Operational complexity: many knobs increase tuning burden. Provide safe-presets and a simple 'balanced' profile for self-serve
notes: Design review 2026-01-22: agreed to move token-bucket funding to steady-state headroom computed from 95th percentile observed concurrency
PM feedback: expose simple preset labeled 'conservative' + 'aggressive' in Console for customers to choose
Follow-up: create runbook for manual credit top-up for enterprise customers during migration windows
SRE requested additional metric: failover_credit_replenishment_rate per-region per-minute
